Build study · Instinct → demonstration → shared judgment

Can Taste Become Institutional Knowledge?

Taste becomes institutional knowledge only when people can examine how a judgment was made, practice it, dispute it, preserve its context, and retain authority over what may be carried.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

Taste is often described as an instinct belonging to one exceptional eye. That description hides the work: looking, comparing, touching, fitting, remembering, rejecting, revising, and learning from skilled collaborators. It also hides unequal access to objects, travel, archives, time, and criticism. An institution should not pretend those conditions are natural talent. It should make the learning pathway and its exclusions visible.

FIT’s patternmaking sources preserve a narrow but useful example of situated professional knowledge: training, slopers, technique, technology, industry practice, and intergenerational experience appear together. UNESCO’s textile safeguarding work adds a crucial boundary—knowledge can belong to practitioners and communities whose consent, benefit, and authority cannot be absorbed into a house manual. Copyright guidance supplies another limit: documenting taste does not make taste itself copyrightable.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · ELICIT

What happened before “I just knew”?

Reconstruct the comparison set, sensory cue, memory, technical constraint, cultural reference, commercial condition, and rejected alternative. Record uncertainty and the contributor who supplied each part of the judgment.

INFERENCES72S73

02 · DEMONSTRATE

Can the judgment be shown in context?

Pair expert demonstration with a learner attempt, correction, second attempt, and commentary on acceptable variation. Some knowledge is tactile, temporal, embodied, confidential, or culturally governed; not everything belongs on camera.

PROPOSALS72S88

03 · CONTEST

Who can say the founder is wrong?

Create a review ritual where pattern, textile, production, wearer, commercial, cultural, accessibility, and archive perspectives can challenge a choice. Preserve the reason for override rather than manufacturing consensus.

PROPOSALS72S76S88

04 · GOVERN

Who may retain and teach it?

Attach consent, compensation, attribution, confidentiality, access, teaching, archive, withdrawal, and cultural-authority fields. Keep protected expression, contract rights, trade secrets, know-how, and abstract taste as separate questions.

VERIFIEDS91S92S88

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Turning taste into institutional knowledge can democratize learning, but it can also extract from workers, communities, and collaborators; privilege what can be verbalized; or make the founder’s preference an unquestionable rule. The system must preserve refusal, disagreement, privacy, and the right not to record.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Choose one recent judgment and reconstruct every comparison, cue, constraint, contributor, and rejected option.
  2. With consent, record demonstration, attempt, correction, variation, and stop condition.
  3. Invite a collaborator to write the strongest disagreement and the conditions under which it should prevail.
  4. Assign consent, compensation, attribution, access, teaching, archive, and withdrawal authority before preservation.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical essay: The Institution Inside the Eye
  • Ten-minute demonstration-and-correction film
  • Eight-frame taste-is-a-process carousel
  • Four tacit-judgment vertical scripts
  • Taste Transmission Protocol
  • Newsletter, oral-history, and workshop editions

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Begin with “I just know.” Rewind the statement into comparison, touch, memory, constraint, contributor, rejection, and correction. End with the right not to record.

02

SHORT 01 — “Taste is not magic. But it is not merely a spreadsheet either.” Show evidence, embodied judgment, and irreducible uncertainty together.

03

SHORT 02 — “The most important institutional field may be disagreement.” Give one collaborator a documented override route.

04

CAROUSEL — ELICIT / DEMONSTRATE / ATTEMPT / CORRECT / COMPARE / CONTEST / CONSENT / GOVERN.

05

AUDIO — A practitioner-led oral-history prompt focused on decisions and boundaries, with pause, embargo, attribution, and withdrawal choices.

06

WORKSHOP — Run one judgment through founder, maker, wearer, accessibility, cultural, and archive lenses; preserve dissent rather than average it away.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
